result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers clearly say no, propose exception-based review, and keep a cancel window before money moves. B states the key point more directly: trust should depend on what is in this run, not on the customer's approval history. It also matches runs against the previous one within tight tolerances and treats the hold window as the main way to recall a bad run. A is strong too, but it frames the problem more around redesigning the review and periodic forced reviews than around comparing this run to the last ones. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say no clearly and propose diff-based relief with a cancel window before the bank file goes out. A is more direct on the key point: it says three approvals only show the review is cheap to pass, and that trust should depend on what is in the run rather than on the customer's history. It is also explicit that the hold before submission is the best recall tool. B's opening line partly treats the streak as evidence the autopilot has been right, although its periodic forced reviews and its clear statement of what evidence would change its view are useful.
